summary: CKGSB's global marketing push is now centred on driving search visibility and leads for Asia Star and the new Intelligent China, while the Knowledge website redesign and a cluster of November events and publications demand attention this week.
summaryDetail: The top priority is the China-based program push agreed at the 30 June strategy meeting: Asia Star and Intelligent China are the lead programs for search and lead generation, with US partner programs (Berkeley, Stanford, Columbia) deliberately on hold. This week the team must launch the Intelligent China webpage and drive traffic, analyse existing Asia Star participant profiles and CRM hot leads, and close out the Google Ads conversion-tracking audit once Joseph's setup brief lands. In parallel, the Knowledge website redesign is moving to execution: keep the current layout with improved menu categorisation, disperse videos by topic, and bring BCI/BSI indices into the section, with Joseph sharing the HTML concept and a 30-minute feedback session before Joker makes the design changes. November deliverables are stacking up — the Q3 2026 Business Sentiment Index awaits professor approval before publication and social promotion, the 13 Nov European Chamber event needs stepped-up executive outreach and updated registration figures from Graeme, and the Women in Leadership Forum needs Ms. Singh's bio and headshot. Also on the near horizon: the warm-up video script review before Moreaid editing, the Sino-Swiss Economic Forum cooperation email, Flow's 2026 website/SEM report discussion with Gontran, and scouting Development Reimagined for China-Africa speakers.

decisions.text: Re-login and update passwords on all devices to prevent repeated account lockouts.
Keep the current Knowledge layout largely as-is rather than a dramatic revamp, with menu categorization as the main improvement.
Remove the standalone videos section and disperse videos by topic across the site.
Use two top menus: School menu at top and Knowledge menu centered.
Bring BCI and BSI indices into the Knowledge section, similar to the school homepage banner.
Do not add a stock-market ticker at the top of the homepage.
Prioritize Asia Star and Intelligent China as the top two programs to promote.
Put US partner programs (Stanford, Columbia) on hold initially; consider Berkeley as a possible third priority.
Focus initial work on China-based programs given stronger demand from overseas executives.
Sarah Kochling will represent CKGSB at the Nov 13 European Chamber Shanghai event
